name: Streamgraph River
summary: An organic streamgraph river where the checkout layer pinches and turns coral after deploy #2231.
look: Warm paper and flowing stacked layers with paper seams, a teal family for healthy streams and coral for the pinched stretch. Italic serif labels live inside the layers; mono time guide and axis.

components.name: Stream layer
components.role: stacked organic band with paper-coloured seams

components.name: Silhouette baseline
components.role: centre-weighted wiggle so the river breathes

components.name: In-stream label
components.role: italic serif name set inside its own layer

components.name: Event guide
components.role: dashed vertical with mono time + deploy id

components.name: Pinch segment
components.role: the anomalous stretch of a layer recoloured coral

motion.name: River scroll
motion.how: whole stream translates left continuously, 1 frame-width per 4 bars (8 s at 120 BPM), linear

motion.name: Swell / thin
motion.how: layer thickness morphs with sine.inOut 1 s (two beats); the teal swell peaks exactly on the drop

motion.name: Pinch
motion.how: coral region wipes downstream from the 09:42 guide with power2.out 0.5 s on the snare

story: Hook: 38 grey dashboard streams with a thin coral thread nobody follows. Drop: the grey layers thin out and one teal stream swells, carrying the Acme mark. Proof: Signups, Active users, Events, Checkout flow on; at 09:42 after deploy #2231 Checkout pinches coral, −18%, Roll back. CTA: a calm teal river, Caught before customers noticed., Start free.
adapt: Stack your product's parallel volumes (traffic sources, job types, plan tiers, model calls) as layers; name them inside the stream and let the anomaly be the one layer that pinches after an event.

references.note: Byron & Wattenberg's streamgraph paper, used by the NYT for 21 years of box office

fit.risk: Streamgraphs are beautiful but hard to read exactly; use them for shape and mood and put the precise number in the card.
